solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Promise to marry novelist after a wager

indicators.note: the novelist's name is placed after the wager in the answer

parts.note: a wager is a bet
Philip Roth, the American novelist

explanation.surface: Someone pledges to wed a writer once a bet has been placed.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to pledge someone in an engagement to wed, a formal promise of marriage.

clue.text: Smell deception involving Welsh diarist

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: the hoax word wraps round the Welsh letter

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or swindle

explanation.surface: A diarist detects the odour of a Welsh trick.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell kept famous journals and wrote the life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell, the Scottish biographer of Dr Johnson, kept celebrated journals and so is a diarist.

clue.text: Watch me cutting it back a bit

indicators.note: me cuts into the other pieces, splitting them
the two letters of it are read backwards

parts.note: a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to watch them trim part of something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb inviting you to look, but it is the noun for a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a portable clock, and a timepiece is any instrument that tells the time.

clue.text: Fellow almost shown up in public

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read bottom to top
the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Trevor is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: A colleague who has nearly been exposed in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TREVOR to TREVO; 'shown up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, not secretly, which is to say done in public.

clue.text: In future try speaking about …

indicators.note: the word for trying a case is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
after can mean about, as in 'ask after someone'

explanation.surface: A promise to attempt to talk about something later on.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAR, as in a judge trying a case, sounds like HERE. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter as an adverb means from now on or at some later time, so in future.

clue.text: Gives testimony showing newspaper boss returns with models

indicators.note: signals that the editor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the editor, ED for short, runs a newspaper
models are people who pose, so poses are what they strike

explanation.surface: A witness explains that a newspaper editor came back accompanied by fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose, in law, is to give sworn evidence, usually in writing or before a court official.

clue.text: … search for Dutch girl around lake

indicators.note: the girl's name goes round the lake letter

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a hunt for a Dutch girl near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig deep or research thoroughly, which is to search.

clue.text: He leads with a horse in form — just the opposite

indicators.note: on its own suggests the horse goes inside the form word
reverses that instruction, so the form word goes inside the horse

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained to pace, a gait used in harness racing
to form something is to make it

explanation.surface: A jockey rides a horse in good form, though the clue then reverses itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' alone would put the horse inside the form word; 'just the opposite' flips the container, so the horse wraps the form word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker is a runner who sets the pace by leading early in a race.

clue.text: Young man saw model home

indicators.note: used as a verb, to model the letters is to shape them anew

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A young man spotted a model at her house.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a country youth or a young suitor.

clue.text: Check to determine support

parts.note: to set a date is to determine it
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: An inspection meant to settle whether to give backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse or hindrance, which is what a check on progress is.

clue.text: Miles covered by a remarkable runner

indicators.note: tells us the miles abbreviation sits inside the word for remarkable

parts.note: 'some' means remarkable, as in 'that was some game'

explanation.surface: A sports report on an athlete who has run a great many miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete but means a river: the Somme flows through northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords often call a river a runner because water runs; the Somme is a French river.

clue.text: Unwilling to bend rule to get Brown into court

indicators.note: bending the word rule twists its letters into a new order
places the brown colour inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone resists bending the regulations just to bring a man called Brown before the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a person's surname being brought to court, but it is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant describes a person who is disinclined or hesitant to do something, so it means unwilling.

clue.text: Go into detail about former head embracing return of old reading aid

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the head word wraps round the reversed reading aid

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: the letters of the reading aid are read backwards

parts.note: ITA, the Initial Teaching Alphabet, was a 1960s scheme for teaching children to read

explanation.surface: A former headteacher discusses at length an outdated method for teaching reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The Initial Teaching Alphabet was a phonetic alphabet used in some British schools in the 1960s and 70s; 'return of' reads its initials backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length, elaborating on a subject in detail.

clue.text: Object about including article on new craze

indicators.note: the reversed goal word holds the article and the new abbreviation
here means turned round, so the goal word is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an article about the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AIM into MIA; 'including' puts AN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is an obsessive enthusiasm, the kind of widespread fad also called a craze.

clue.text: Refuse to bear rector's suggestive looks

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the dregs word carries the rector's letter inside

parts.note: lees are the dregs or sediment left in wine, so refuse
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put up with the vicar's knowing glances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Leers are sly, lascivious or knowing looks, the sort called suggestive.

clue.text: Spread of latest lie is dependent on another

indicators.note: spreading the words out lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: The newest falsehood circulates, relying on some other source.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite state or body depends on a more powerful one, orbiting or serving it.

clue.text: Consider translation of Kant as a source of ideas

parts.note: to consider is to think

indicators.note: translating the philosopher's name is taken as changing his letters about

explanation.surface: A suggestion to reflect on a version of the German philosopher's work as inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is a body of experts set up to produce ideas and policy proposals.

clue.text: Lestrade for instance is concerned with power in part

parts.note: in means engaged in, as in 'he is in insurance'

indicators.note: the power letter goes into the part word

parts.note: a sector is a part or division

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes character is described as working in some field of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lestrade is the Scotland Yard detective in the Sherlock Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade of Scotland Yard is an example of a police officer of that rank.

clue.text: A deep love of America shown by Ford's last speech

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the name Ford

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: President Ford's final address expressed a deep affection for the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is intense love and admiration, so it means deep love.

clue.text: Upsets remaining performers

parts.note: over means left or remaining, as in 'food left over'
a turn is a variety act or performer

explanation.surface: Upsetting news about the acts still left on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Overturns as a verb means knocks over or reverses, which is to upset something.

clue.text: Working with Norm to frame exercises in writing

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the norm word goes round the exercises letters like a frame

parts.note: par is the norm or standard level
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Someone works out with a man named Norm, setting the exercises down on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper means written down, as opposed to spoken or merely thought.

clue.text: Crosses road carrying ducks before first of shots

indicators.note: the road abbreviation holds the ducks' letters inside

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and O looks like nought, so ducks gives two Os

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word shots

explanation.surface: Ducks cross a road before the first shots ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' reads as a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen, so roods are crosses.

clue.text: Ready to ride in charge at start of Derby

definitions.text: Ready to ride in charge at start of Derby

parts.words: Ready to ride in charge at start of Derby
parts.note: a horse is ready to be ridden once tack is put on; being burdened with a duty also uses this word

explanation.surface: A horse being prepared for the big race at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is the famous flat horse race at Epsom in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with its seat strapped on is ready for a rider, and a person made responsible is likewise charged with something.

clue.text: Left by a detective to protect the Queen from danger

indicators.note: the detective letters surround and so shield the Queen's letters

parts.note: PI is a private investigator
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A private eye stays behind to guard the monarch from harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious and immediate danger, the two words being close synonyms.

clue.text: Sources also turned up in the centre of Warsaw

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the central letters
takes the two middle letters of the city's name
in a down answer the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Origins that also emerged in the heart of the Polish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes OOT from TOO; 'the centre of' Warsaw gives RS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roots are origins or sources, as in the roots of a problem.

clue.text: Musicians form it for support after soprano joins large company

indicators.note: the support word follows the soprano letter

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a band is a company or group of people

explanation.surface: A soprano joins a big company of performers, who need a stand of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' simply links the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a group of musicians playing steel drums, Caribbean in origin.

clue.text: Writer found in street exhausted

indicators.note: places the writing tool inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A tired author is discovered lying in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up or worn out, which is to say exhausted.

clue.text: Become less ambivalent at the end over supporting the French

indicators.note: in a down answer, the later pieces sit below and so support the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: takes the last letter of ambivalent

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: An undecided person eventually supports the French side.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to ease off or diminish, so to become less intense.

clue.text: Standing out in favour of conservationists maintaining colliery

indicators.note: the in-favour word plus the charity's letters hold the colliery word

parts.note: pro means in favour of
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone stands out for backing conservationists who want to keep a coal pit open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintaining' asks the first two pieces together to hold the colliery word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent projects from its surroundings or is conspicuous, so it is standing out.

clue.text: Test of hearing

definitions.meaning: a case heard before a court of law

explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both an experiment that tests something and a court case that hears evidence.

clue.text: Peter's worried about cocaine in particular

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the drug's letter
the man's name is worried into a different order of its letters

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A man named Peter frets about a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges PETERS (the apostrophe is ignored) into RESPET, which goes 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect can mean a detail or aspect, as in 'in every respect', so a particular.

clue.text: Expressed discontent long after soldiers died

indicators.note: the longing word comes after the soldiers' letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to long for something is to pine
D is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they yearned long after the troops were killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so repined means grumbled or showed discontent.
